summary: `-np` defaults to -1 (auto). With auto slots the server picked 4 slots and `kv_unified = true` in a b9354 log.

facts.text: `-np` defaults to -1 (auto). With auto slots the server picked 4 slots and `kv_unified = true` in a b9354 log.
Under unified KV every slot reports the full pool size (`n_ctx = 32768` for four slots on `--ctx-size 32768`), because any one request can use the whole pool.
`--kv-unified-per-slot N` is a newer flag: it sets a per-slot context limit; with no `-c` it sizes the shared pool as `n_parallel * N`.
Slot choice for a new task: LRU when nothing matches, otherwise the slot with the best longest-common-prefix similarity above `--slot-prompt-similarity` (0.10).
Context checkpoints (`-ctxcp`) are per slot, so checkpoint memory scales with the slot count.
2026-02 (issue 19523): unified KV with several slots found to slow decode on CUDA; Vulkan had a regression fixed within two days.
2026-08 (PR 27496): `--fit` made aware of `n_streams` so non-unified KV with several slots gets full per-slot context; draft/MTP context now follows the target context.
With `-kvu --parallel 4`, inactive slots that still hold a populated prompt slowed token generation of the active slot on CUDA; prompt processing was unaffected; slowdown persisted until restart.
Under `--fit -no-kvu -np 4` before PR 27496, each slot got `n_ctx_train / 4`; a draft context sized from `n_ctx_train / n_streams` could overflow when a slot filled, returning HTTP 500.

Maintainer position (19523): unified KV is poorly supported on CUDA, so either disable it and pay the memory, or run `-np 1`. Router-mode users still run `--parallel 4 --kv-unified` with a per-slot limit (29322). Neither side has Metal measurements.
Whether Metal flash attention skips masked blocks under unified KV, i.e. whether the 19523 slowdown exists on Apple GPUs.
Whether `--kv-unified-per-slot` changes fit or checkpoint accounting on a Mac.
The server README lists `-np, --parallel N` as number of server slots with default -1 meaning auto.

The server README documents `--kv-unified-per-slot N` (env `LLAMA_ARG_KV_UNIFIED_PER_SLOT`): context limit per parallel slot, default unset, and when set without `-c` the shared KV pool is sized `n_parallel*N`.
The README states `-ctxcp` is the maximum number of context checkpoints created per slot and also answers to the alias `--swa-checkpoints`.
A b9354 server log reads `n_parallel is set to auto, using n_parallel = 4 and kv_unified = true`.
In that log, all four slots print `new slot, n_ctx = 32768` while `--ctx-size 32768` was the whole pool, so under unified KV each slot reports the pool size.
The same log shows slot choice `selected slot by LRU, t_last = -1` for the first request and `selected slot by LCP similarity, sim_best = 0.928 (> 0.100 thold), f_keep = 0.911` for the follow-up.

Issue 19523 (b7974, Windows, `-kvu --parallel 4 --ctx-size 196608`, Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B) reports that populated inactive slots (`is_processing: false`) lower token-generation speed of the active slot, that prompt processing is unaffected, and that the slowdown grows over the first four requests as blank slots fill and stays until restart.
In 19523 ggerganov answers that the unified KV cache is not well supported by the CUDA backend and offers two options: disable unified KV and accept the memory cost, or use one slot (`-np 1`).

In 19523 the Vulkan case (AMD Strix Halo, Windows) was a regression from mask-loading changes (PR 19281) that stopped skipping masked -INF blocks in `-kvu` mode; PR 19582 restored it and the reporter confirmed the fix on 2026-02-14.
A 2026-07-23 comment on 19523 says a four-A100 host serving a Qwen3.6-27B GGUF with llama-server hangs and performs poorly under multiple connections.
PR 27496 (merged 2026-08-22 as commit 2fb989b) changes `--fit -no-kvu -np 4` so `n_ctx` becomes `n_ctx_train * 4` (524288 in the tinygemma3 test) and each slot gets 131072 instead of 32768.

The same commit makes the server's draft context follow the target context: with non-unified KV the target held `n_ctx_train` per sequence while the draft context fell back to `n_ctx_train / n_streams`, and a slot filled past that made the draft batch fail to decode and the server answer 500.
The same commit makes fit measure a draft or MTP model's memory at the largest context the target can take, because that memory grows with context and a fixed byte margin cannot express it.

Inferred: for a single-user agent on a Mac, `--parallel 1` removes slot-selection, per-slot checkpoint multiplication and unified-KV tradeoffs at once; two of the working 24055 configurations use `--parallel 1`.
